papers.title: Curvature-Aware Edge Dynamic GNNs for Low-$p_T$ Track Reconstruction at HL-LHC
papers.abstract: Particle track reconstruction in high-energy collider experiments is a computationally demanding combinatorial problem, traditionally solved by Kalman filters that scale poorly with increasing detector occupancy. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative. In this work, we introduce the Manifold Helical-IN, a novel Interaction Network architecture that explicitly embeds detector spacepoints onto a helical manifold chart using curvature-aware features. This geometric projection mathematically unrolls the tightly curling trajectories of low-momentum particles. Consequently, the network can distinguish true physical tracks from combinatorial noise with good precision. Evaluated on the TrackML challenge dataset, the proposed Manifold Helical-IN achieves a reconstruction efficiency of 0.9675 in the experimentally critical $p_T > 0.5$ GeV regime, approaching recently reported Transformer-based approaches. Crucially, the manifold embedding yields a fake track rate of 0.0037. This represents a 13-fold improvement over the baseline Helical-IN (0.0508). Furthermore, the model maintains good track coherence, as quantified by our proposed Mean Hit Recovery Fraction (MHRF) of 0.858, and achieves a highly efficient inference latency of approximately 150 ms per event on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. These results represent a critical step toward real-time soft particle tracking for the High-Level Trigger (HLT). By operating within practical HLT latency budgets, this geometry-aware approach provides a pathway to recover soft, anomalous Beyond Standard Model signatures such as unclustered energy patterns (SUEPs), that routinely evade standard hardware filters.

papers.title: Waveform-based pulse timing enhanced by self-supervised neural regression models for digital nuclear instrumentation
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of high-sampling-rate digital nuclear devices, their applications in nuclear facilities and related fields become more acceptable, and will possibly become widespread due to the versatility and flexibility of waveform sampling systems. When digitizers reach hundreds of megahertz or gigahertz, their lower limit in time measurement probes into the sub-nanosecond region, expediting their use in a bunch of time-critical scenarios. While conventional algorithms coupled with digital sampling techniques realize fair pulse timing in certain conditions, the potentials are still open to compact and efficient machine learning models. In this paper, we intend to boost the performance of pulse timing with a new paradigm of self-supervised learning on matched waveform pairs. The proposed method combines the mainstream self-supervised loss and the auxiliary weakly-supervised loss on the reference set, jointly improving the timing performance. We apply the method in a gamma/neutron-mixed radiation field, common in nuclear facilities. The simulation and experimental results show that, the proposed method not only outperforms conventional timing algorithms, but also surpasses neural network models based on supervised learning alone. Considering the trained model is lightweight and computationally efficient, it is promising to deploy it on edge devices, like economical microcontrollers with neural processing units.

papers.title: BeST: Beta splatted tomography for direct reconstruction from coherent imaging measurements
papers.abstract: Conventional coherent X-ray tomography requires the phase of each projection to be reconstructed with high fidelity. However, individual reconstructed projections might be flawed, e.g. due to positioning errors, yielding inconsistent tomographic reconstructions. By directly coupling phase retrieval and tomography, consistency is enforced through a common object volume. But reconstructing a full volume demands substantial computational resources. To reduce this demand, we introduce Beta Splatted Tomography (BeST), which represents the common object volume using compactly supported beta primitives with closed-form analytical projections, enabling efficient reconstruction directly from coherent scattering images. This representation substantially reduces the number of optimizable parameters compared to a voxel grid. We demonstrate BeST on experimental datasets from hard X-ray near-field holography and far-field ptychography measurements. In both cases, the joint technique improves reconstruction quality compared to two-step methods.

papers.title: Learning transferable event representations for charmed baryon physics at BESIII
papers.abstract: Deep learning has become an essential tool in high-energy physics, where the ability to learn transferable event representations can significantly improve model generalization across related physics processes. In this work, we present a Particle Transformer-based framework for learning such representations for charmed baryon physics in the BESIII experiment. The framework is implemented through large-scale pre-training on Monte Carlo simulation samples and subsequent fine-tuning for downstream analyses. Using the production and decays of the charmed baryon $\Lambda_c^+$ as a benchmark, we develop pre-trained models for both event classification and momentum-direction regression. The classification model learns discriminative event representations for the dominant physics categories, rejecting $96.90\%$ of background events at a signal efficiency of 90.00\%. Across 12 benchmark $\Lambda_c^+$ decay channels, fine-tuning from the pre-trained model achieves performance comparable to or better than training from scratch, with particularly clear improvements in low-statistics regimes. For the regression task, the pre-trained model improves the average angular resolutions across the same benchmark channels. Further improvement is obtained after fine-tuning in the representative semileptonic decay $\Lambda_c^+ \to p K^- e^+ \nu_e$. In addition, the predicted momentum direction enables reconstruction of the parent kinematics without a recoil-side tag and thereby increases signal efficiency. For this semileptonic decay, the pre-trained regression model increases the signal efficiency by approximately one order of magnitude relative to the double-tag method. This strategy provides a scalable solution for a wide range of physics cases at BESIII and can be extended to other high energy experiments.

papers.title: Bayesian Transfer Operators in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
papers.abstract: Transfer operators provide a linear description of nonlinear dynamical systems by propagating observables or probability distributions. In reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, these operators are represented through conditional mean embeddings, whose regularized estimator coincides with the posterior mean of Gaussian process regression. Building on this correspondence, we formulate Gaussian Process Dynamic Mode Decomposition, a Bayesian transfer-operator method that combines sparse variational Gaussian processes with kernel-based Koopman and Perron--Frobenius operator approximation. The resulting framework provides a principled route to uncertainty quantification, scalable sparse approximations, and data-adaptive dictionary learning for prediction and spectral analysis. Additionally, the model-selection formulation naturally gives rise to a forward--backward operator structure, which establishes a connection between Bayesian transfer-operator learning and time-lagged canonical correlation analysis.

papers.title: Amortized Inference of Multi-Modal Posteriors using Likelihood-Weighted Normalizing Flows
papers.abstract: We present a technique for posterior estimation using Normalizing Flows trained with likelihood-weighted importance sampling, the special case of neural importance sampling in which the proposal is the prior. This approach allows for the efficient inference of theoretical parameters in high-dimensional inverse problems without the need for posterior training samples. We implement the method on multi-modal benchmark tasks in 2D and 3D to check for the efficacy. A critical observation of our study is the impact of the base distribution on the modelled posteriors. We find that standard unimodal base distributions leave spurious probability \textit{bridges} between well-separated modes. We demonstrate that initializing the flow with a Gaussian Mixture Model that matches the number of target modes significantly improves reconstruction fidelity, as measured by some distance and divergence metrics. Finally, we apply this method to a curated problem in heavy flavour physics --- the extraction of the Wolfenstein parameters from the CP asymmetry in $B^0\to J/\psi\,K^0$; it is multimodal, non-Gaussian, and asymmetric in its mode weights --- and compare the results against a well-converged Markov Chain Monte Carlo reference and an exact reference computed by quadrature, using different metrics. Used as a proposal for importance sampling, the trained flow removes its remaining bias and gives the evidence.
